meta.title: Amharic Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 200 phrases and sentences · 13 phrases, 187 sentences · both directions
meta.desc: Amharic said whole: greetings, the phrasebook questions a visitor needs, wishes, exclamations, a proverb and a set of short everyday sentences. Both study directions, each a card of its own: Amharic → English and English → Amharic. 13 PHRASES are every phrase, interjection and proverb English Wiktionary has for Amharic that the level decks do not teach, with Wiktionary's own meaning and romanisation: ጤና ይስጥልኝ 'hello', ሀሎ on the phone, እሺ 'okay', ስምህ ማን ነው? 'what is your name?' and እንግሊዝኛ ትችላለህ? 'do you speak English?' — each in the forms Amharic uses for a man, a woman or politely — መልካም ልደት 'happy birthday', መልካም አዲስ አመት 'happy New Year', and the proverb ሮም በአንድ ቀን አልተገነባችም 'Rome wasn't built in a day'. 187 SENTENCES are Tatoeba's short Amharic sentences (nine words at most) with their English translation, printed as Tatoeba has them, each card giving the sentence's Tatoeba number. Amharic marks who is spoken to, so where two sentences share an English one the card says which is said to a man, to a woman, politely or to several people. They carry no romanisation (Tatoeba gives none): the Fidäl deck teaches the letters. THE DECK IS SMALL BECAUSE THE SOURCES ARE: Wiktionary files eight Amharic entries as phrases or proverbs, and Tatoeba holds about 250 Amharic sentences with a translation, so nothing here is invented and nothing is padded. It is not a CEFR level; ይቅርታ 'sorry' is in A1, and nothing the level decks teach is repeated. There is no speaker button: few devices have an Amharic voice. Sources: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0); Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
